newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits steady to easier before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits steady to easier before FOMC.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were steady to easier in thin trade with most traders sidelined before today's first leg of a two-day meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy setting body, dealers said on Tuesday.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet on February 4 and 5 to discuss the future of the country's monetary policy. The Fed is expected to announce the results on Wednesday.
The market is also waiting for today's issue of the U.S. December new home sales and leading indicators data.
New home sales for December are forecast to be around 745,000 units compared with 772,000 units reported in November.
December leading indicators are expected to be unchanged from November's 0.1 percent gain.

"Rates were steady to a little bit softer this morning on some position adjustments. There was little impact from Monday's NAPM index, personal income/consumption and construction spending data and most people were sidelined," a local dealer said.
"All eyes are on today's FOMC meeting although most people are not expecting any change in interest rates," he said.

"But everyone will be waiting for the results on Wednesday, even if there's no change. The new homes sales and leading indicators figures will probably be non-events, but the next key indicator on the economy will come out on Friday when the January employment report is released," he added.
In short dates, Tuesday/Wednesday eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed were unchanged from Monday's common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.
Among term rates, two-months was unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent.
